answer.evidence: Rows 0-4 and 8-12 are light snow treads seen from above, each ending in a dark front-edge line (rows 5 and 13) followed by dark riser or shadow rows (5-7 and 13-15). That gives two foreshortened steps climbing north. Rows 16-31 are a flat brown-grey vertical cliff face, 16 rows tall. The silhouette is 32 wide in every row, with no receding side face. It reads as a 3/4-view stair cut into a cliff.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 9 visible tones per tile, above the grass reference (3) and the paving reference (7). Its 39% near-flat coverage is far above both references (0%), and the picture shows why. The lower beige/pink block is one nearly flat colour with no grain, speckle or per-stone variation. The snow band and the steps read as only about 3 lightness steps (white, pale blue, grey-blue), where Beodeul materials carry 5-6. The 0% neutral dark edge share means the outlines are tinted, not near-black, which is a point in its favour. Even so, the large flat fills and the shallow ramps leave it flatter and more sticker-like than the references, which have grain on every area. A careful artist would not accept it next to them.
